title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.

bite.hook: A new construction of 'quantum many-body scars' creates coherent energy oscillations across two coupled systems.
tldr: Researchers constructed approximate many-body scar states by coupling two copies of a quantum system using a bilocal size interaction.
They identified specific Krylov basis states that remain concentrated in a single size sector in the thermodynamic limit.
The resulting system exhibits a tower of equally spaced energy levels, leading to collective oscillations of energy between the copies.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum scars are rare states that defy standard thermalization, potentially offering a way to store quantum information longer without it dissipating into heat.
bite.eli5: Imagine two identical swings connected by a rubber band. Usually, if you push one, the energy spreads out randomly. These 'scars' are like a special trick where the energy keeps bouncing back and forth between the two swings in a perfect, repeating pattern instead of dying out.

glossary.shortDef: Non-thermal states in quantum systems that avoid the usual rapid spread of information.
glossary.eli5Def: Special quantum states that stay organized and don't turn into chaotic heat, like a memory that refuses to fade.

glossary.shortDef: A set of states generated by repeatedly applying a Hamiltonian to an initial state.
glossary.eli5Def: A way of organizing quantum states by seeing how they evolve step-by-step under a specific rule.
